verbatim: So read replicas, sharding, and then you go into multi-master if you want to make things overtly complicated.

statement: Whether the proxy is layer 4 or layer 7 does not matter for long-lived connections when it is only relaying messages back and forth: in the end the data passes through it. That pure relaying is what is done in most such cases.
detail: Student 2 argued it depends: with an L4 proxy it is like a single tunnel to the server, and an L7 LB can make intelligent decisions. Teacher: does not matter if only relaying.
speaker: teacher
verbatim: if you're only routing the messages here and there, it really does not matter. And if it's layer four or layer seven

statement: A layer 7 load balancer can make intelligent routing decisions (unlike a pure L4 tunnel).
speaker: student (proposal)
verbatim: if we have a kind of layer seven load balancer, then it can make intelligent decision.

statement: Avoid generic statements about tools ('X does not support Y'): tools keep gaining features, so there is no hard and fast rule; check the specific current capabilities.
speaker: teacher
verbatim: So generic statements are typically tend to avoid.

statement: MongoDB originally did not want ACID properties but now supports ACID, so saying 'MongoDB' or 'NoSQL does not support ACID' is wrong.
speaker: teacher
verbatim: if I say that MongoDB does not support ACID, that would be wrong. Or NoSQL does not support ACID, that is wrong.

statement: Kafka now has a broadcast capability that solves a kind of real-time pub/sub use case, so one cannot simply say Kafka does not support real-time pub/sub.
speaker: teacher
verbatim: basically Kafka broadcast is there, which solves kind of real-time Pub/Sub use case.

statement: Databases are converging and look alike nowadays: MySQL and Postgres support JSON, MongoDB supports ACID, wide-column stores support ACID compliance, Hudi supports transactions; everyone does everything because building is easy.
speaker: teacher
verbatim: all databases are converging to being exactly. They look like one of them nowadays.
